defect_observations.observation: The constant term of the exact square identity is asserted to agree 'after putting them over tau^2 s^2 (tau^2+s^2)'; the algebra is not displayed. The method is stated and the identity was rechecked by this auditor, so it is recorded as a terse written step, not a sketch. Non-blocking.

The future-draw mechanism (conditionally independent Bernoulli(theta) draws, independent of the past given theta) is conveyed only by 'further draws'. The annex states it explicitly (lines 242-243), and C011 states its analogue in the theorem (line 291). Read as stated by reference to the opening hypothesis. Non-blocking.

Two steps are left implicit: joint measurability of the transported likelihood f~ (immediate from measurability of g^{-1}), and the off-G case of Pi~_x = g_#Pi_x (immediate from m~ = m and the convention Pi_x = Pi off G). Non-blocking.
Only the right side's integral over G^c is said to vanish. The matching vanishing of Pi(A)m(x) over B intersect G^c follows from the same bound but is not written. Non-blocking.

The contamination paragraph does not restate that x is regular for Pi (m(x) finite). The proof (annex lines 426-427) uses m(x)Pi_x(A) = integral over A of f dPi. Read as carried over from 'At a regular observation' (line 326). Non-blocking.

The body calls -log m_n the cumulative conditional logarithmic score, a loss orientation. The held K&R sec. 3.2 (txt 355-366, p. 777) defines LS = sum log pr-hat_i(y_i) = +log pr(D|H_k). No orientation crosswalk is given. This is not misattributed, since the body does not ascribe this orientation to the source. Non-blocking.

The claim that the sensitivity and interpretation sections supply 'exact examples for the distinctions in their Sections 5 and 8.2' carries no \cite locator; only line 15 cites the work. Checked at the held source: sec. 5.1 (p. 781) discusses parameterization-dependent prior prescriptions via conditioning on psi=psi0 (a Borel-paradox case). C012 instead gives an exact example of the same distinction for uniform priors, and sec. 5.2 Eq. (14) is the approximate counterpart of C013's exact identity. The attribution is supported as a claim about distinctions, not reproductions.
